questions.prompt: Besides making code from a frame, what does Figma say its MCP server lets agents do?

options.text: Write native Figma content back to the canvas, not only read from it
options.explanation: Right. Figma says the server also lets agents write native Figma content back to the canvas.

options.text: Only read files, because the server cannot change anything on canvas
options.explanation: Figma says the server also lets agents write native Figma content back to the canvas.

options.text: Run only on a designer's laptop, because no remote version is offered
options.explanation: Figma strongly recommends its remote server. A desktop version also exists.

questions.prompt: Why does OpenAI suggest the allowed_tools setting?

options.text: It makes the model write longer, more careful answers about each tool
options.explanation: The setting is about which tools are imported, not answer length.

options.text: A long list can mean high cost and latency, so import only the tools you need
options.explanation: Right. OpenAI says exposing many tools can result in high cost and latency.

options.text: It lets the server skip OAuth, so that nobody at the studio has to sign in
options.explanation: It has nothing to do with sign-in. It filters tools.

questions.prompt: What does the allowed_tools field do in Gemini's Remote MCP settings?

options.text: It adds new tools to the server from the studio's own list
options.explanation: It narrows the server's tools. It does not add tools.

options.text: It sets the HTTP headers that are sent with each request
options.explanation: Headers are a separate field in the same table.

options.text: It restricts which tools from the server the agent may call
options.explanation: Right. Google's field table says it restricts which tools from the server the agent may call.
